name: Multiple GitHub accounts
goalName: Create a way to easily toggle the account for repositories
goal: As I have a Fontys account and a personal account on GitHub, I need to be able to toggle accounts for repositories. While working on two projects simultaneously (one for school, one personal), the right account needs to show up for commits.

approach.text: To get an understanding of how git stores the credentials, I created repositories in Chrome (school account) and Edge (personal account). I added a first commit in the school repository, where I noticed my personal account showed up as the one which commited. When I tried to push to the personal repository, I got an error saying the repository was not found. I knew that the credentials were stored in the Credential Manager, so I deleted that entry and made a second commit. Not having a password set, git asked me for my password or a token. I decided to create tokens for both accounts and used them to push the second commit. Unfortunately, in both repositories, my personal account still showed up as the one which commited.

I decided to look up how other people removed their credentials, and came across the following source: <<source Zafar, B. R. (n.d.). How to Remove Credentials From Git in Windows. https://linuxhint.com/remove-credentials-from-git-windows/.>> It suggested to use "git config --global --unset credential.helper" After a third commit, the issue still was not resolved.

The source gave me an idea how git worked. I remembered having to set my name and email globally in previous semesters. After using "git config --global --unset user.name" and "git config --global --unset user.email", it prompted me to enter my name and email. My name could be the same, so I set it using the global tag. For the email, I set it locally without the global tag, meaning that I have to set my email for every repository's first commit, a solution acceptable for me.

normalLearnings: I know how git stores credentials.
I know how to set credentials both locally and globally.
I know how to clear a field using --unset
result: After a fourth commit, the accounts showed up as expected as seen in the picture below: <<image 2.png>> The name 454406 is due to the account on GitHub itself having that set as its name.
validation: As seen in the picture, the different repositories have a different email set, and the commits are made by two separate accounts.
contribution: Being able to set an account per repository helps keeping projects managable and separated.
